Why WWT?

World Wide Technology (WWT) strives to make a new world happen. WWT's work benefits clients and partners as much as it does its people and community across the globe.

Founded in 1990, WWT brings together strategy, deep technical expertise and world-class partnerships to help public and private sector organizations design, build and scale intelligent AI, digital, cybersecurity, cloud and infrastructure solutions. Through its Advanced Technology Center (ATC)—a collaborative ecosystem featuring state-of-the-art hardware and software—WWT enables clients and partners to conceptualize, test and validate innovative technology and then deploy solutions at scale using its global integration and distributions capabilities.

With more than 14,000 team members and over 60 locations globally, WWT's culture—grounded in core values and leadership philosophies—has been recognized by Fortune® and Great Place to Work for its commitment to innovation, trust and creating a great place to work for all. WWT provides products and services to large enterprise, global service provider and public sector clients in up to 130 countries across six continents. Softchoice, a World Wide Technology company, supports commercial and SMB markets in the U.S. and Canada.

Want to work with highly motivated individuals on high-performance teams? Join WWT today!

Job Summary

The Microsoft Frontier SSA is a presales technical strategist and hands-on AI solution architect who helps customers identify, prioritize, and prototype high-value AI use cases. This role blends customer-facing advisory skills with practical engineering capability across agent strategy, Copilot extensibility, AI application development, and developer productivity. The successful candidate will guide executive and technical stakeholders through AI opportunity discovery, solution envisioning, architecture design, and rapid prototyping that demonstrates what is possible with Microsoft Copilot Studio, AI Foundry, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Power Platform, and Azure AI services.

Demonstrate how GitHub Copilot can accelerate software development, modernization, documentation, test creation, and developer workflow transformation.
Facilitate workshops with business, IT, security, and developer stakeholders to prioritize AI use cases, assess readiness, define success measures, and identify prototype candidates.
Support executive conversations on Microsoft AI strategy, ROI, responsible AI, data readiness, governance, security, extensibility, and organizational adoption.
Partner with sales, solution architecture, delivery, and Microsoft teams to shape opportunities, create differentiated solution narratives, and transition successful prototypes into funded engagements.

jobs.title: Sr. AI Solution Architect
jobs.description:
Cohesity is a leader in AI-powered data security and management. Aided by an extensive ecosystem of partners, Cohesity makes it easy to secure, protect, manage, and get value from data — across the data center, edge, and cloud. Cohesity helps organizations defend against cybersecurity threats with comprehensive data security and management capabilities, including immutable backup snapshots, AI-based threat detection, monitoring for malicious behavior, and rapid recovery at scale.

We’ve been named a Leader by multiple analyst firms and have been globally recognized for Innovation, Product Strength, and Simplicity in Design.

Join us on our mission to shape the future of our industry.

GAIA is Cohesity’s enterprise AI platform for unlocking the value of unstructured data across the Cohesity Data Cloud. It helps customers securely search, understand, summarize, and reason across current and historical enterprise information, while preserving permissions, provenance, and governance. GAIA also provides a foundation for agentic AI by making trusted enterprise context available to AI applications, copilots, and agents — helping customers move from simply protecting data to using it as a strategic source of intelligence and action.

Why Now

These are founding seats in Cohesity’s new AI Business Unit. GAIA is where the market is heading — enterprises secured their data with us; now they want to activate it for AI. You’ll help build the technical sales playbook on top of 13,600 existing customers and co-sell muscle from NVIDIA and the hyperscalers, proving what GAIA can do in the accounts that matter most. Ground floor, executive air cover from the GM of AI, and a partner ecosystem already generating pipeline.

You are the technical engine behind the AI sales motion. Paired with the Specialist Account Executive, AI, you own the technical win — the AE owns the commercial relationship and the number, and you make the technology real: architecture, demos, POCs, and the credibility to hold a technical room. This is a pre-sales, business-value, and consultative solutions role, not a hands-on production-engineering seat. You bring enough depth to design and defend a solution, and enough range to translate it into a value story an executive buys.

HOW YOU’LL SPEND YOUR TIME HERE:

Own the technical win in every GAIA deal you support — discovery, solution design, demos, and proof of value — partnered with the Specialist AE who owns the commercial close.
Be the AI subject-matter expert in the room on data architecture, RAG, deployment models, and where the risk sits — credible enough to hold a technical conversation with a CAIO, CDO, VP of AI, or their architects.
Design and deliver enterprise-grade AI/GenAI solutions integrated with Cohesity’s data security and management platform, leveraging our unique access to enterprise backup, archive, and unstructured data.
Architect retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) solutions and build reference architectures, solution accelerators, and demos that connect Cohesity’s core strengths with emerging AI capabilities.
Lead technical workshops, POCs, and pilots that validate AI use cases across regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, public sector, legal) and turn a first proof point into a multi-phase plan.
Build executive-quality technical narratives — solution briefs, architecture diagrams, and business cases specific to the account, not a template with a logo swapped in.
Work the AI partner ecosystem — NVIDIA, the hyperscalers, and infrastructure OEMs — on joint solutions, technical co-sell, and reference architectures that accelerate deals.
Feed the field back into the roadmap — partner with Product and Engineering so what you learn in deals shapes what we build and how customers adopt it.
Support disciplined deal hygiene — accurate technical qualification, honest POC exit criteria, and forecasts the AE and the business can plan against.

The Role

This is a client-facing technical role at the intersection of customers, product, and applied AI. You'll work directly with American manufacturers to understand how their business operates, turn messy requirements into clear agent behaviors, and deploy a reliable Frank that delivers measurable value.

You'll own customer agent deployments end-to-end: map workflows, prioritize requirements, write SOPs and prompts, build evals, configure tools and guardrails, launch with users, and improve performance over time. The inputs are real and imperfect: dirty PDFs, legacy data, tribal knowledge, and edge cases that break naive systems.

The work is hands-on, fast-moving, and deeply user-centric. You'll work with LLMs and code every day, communicate directly with customer teams, and turn what you learn in the field into better product capabilities and a faster, more repeatable deployment system.

What You’ll Do

Lead agent deployments from discovery and requirements scoping through configuration, go-live, quantified ROI, and ongoing improvement
Map complex customer workflows and turn them into focused requirements, SOPs, prompts, tools, guardrails, approvals, and handoffs
Build evals and test cases that measure agent quality, expose failure modes, and guide iteration
Configure and launch agents, monitor their real-world performance, investigate failures, and improve reliability over time
Run customer workshops, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and close every dependency and follow-up needed to keep deployments moving
Learn complex customer domains quickly and advocate for customer needs with product and engineering
Turn repeated deployment problems into reusable patterns, tooling, and product improvements that make future launches faster

Who you are

You have 4+ years of experience in software engineering or a client-facing technical role such as forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or implementation consulting
You are technically strong and comfortable writing code, prompting LLMs, building evals, and learning new agent-engineering techniques
You can scope ambiguous requirements, prioritize aggressively, and design a simple solution within real product and operational constraints
You are an exceptional communicator who can run a customer workshop, present with confidence, and build trust from the shop floor to the executive team
You are highly organized and process-oriented: you can manage multiple deployments, track details, use metrics, and close every loop
You learn complex domains quickly and combine customer empathy with a product mindset, turning field insights into better tools and experiences
You are ambitious, resourceful, action-oriented, and team-first; you care about strengthening American manufacturing and are excited to work in person five days a week in NYC and travel to customer sites across the US

Bonus points

Experience building and operating agentic systems in production
Experience in manufacturing or another industrial or operationally complex setting
Experience creating SOPs or leading change-management work
Experience integrating and deploying third-party APIs or legacy systems

About Forgepoint

Revitalize an industry. Rebuild America's manufacturing backbone.

America builds satellites, jet engines, and semiconductors with world-class precision, but the software running factory offices is decades behind. Estimators, procurement teams, and accountants still lose hours to spreadsheets, PDFs, and manual data entry.

Forgepoint builds AI workers for back office departments like quoting, purchasing, invoicing, and sales coordination. By removing back-office bottlenecks, we help US manufacturers move faster, grow, and compete globally.

We're backed by a16z speedrun and angels from Brex, Xwing, and Betterment. Join us in rebuilding the digital foundation of American manufacturing.

Jack Strauss
— Co-Founder & CEO

Jack began his career at Acer and Northrop Grumman, then advised industrial companies at Bain. At Xwing, he helped scale the company and led GTM through its acquisition by Joby Aviation. He holds an MBA from Stanford and a BA from USC.

In person every day in NYC for high-bandwidth collaboration
Talk to users constantly: we build with manufacturers, not for them
Own outcomes end-to-end and drive solutions without waiting for permission

There's Always a Way: We are relentlessly resourceful, take ownership of constraints, and find a path forward when others stop.

jobs.title: Research Scientist – Computer Vision (Body Pose Detection)v1
jobs.description:
About Mecka AI

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

The Role

While our existing perception division handles state estimation and spatial mapping, this role is dedicated to one of the most critical bottlenecks in embodied AI: full-body kinematics, human locomotion, and human-scene interaction. We are hiring a Research Scientist to architect and train proprietary foundation models from scratch focused on 3D human body tracking and articulated pose estimation.

Your core mandate is twofold: building our in-house equivalents to cutting-edge 3D human body and mesh recovery architectures, and developing highly robust interaction models tailored for complex, real-world environments characterized by severe occlusions and dynamic motion. Beyond these core pillars, you will serve as a lead problem-solver for emergent perception challenges as our hardware and downstream robotics needs evolve.

To achieve this, we can provide a massive, continuous stream of high-quality, proprietary ground-truth human motion data captured by our infrastructure. You will use this data advantage to train networks that surpass current public baselines, owning the complete human-scene perception loop for our data engine.

What You'll Work On

Architecting Proprietary Articulation Models

Zero-to-One Model Development: Design, implement, and train state-of-the-art networks for 3D human pose estimation, dense full-body mesh recovery, and kinematic tracking.
Large-Scale Distributed Training: Scale multi-view and temporal ML architectures across multi-GPU clusters to handle massive, multi-modal datasets of humans navigating and interacting with their environments.
Loss & Architecture Innovation: Push the boundaries of current paradigms by developing novel loss functions that enforce biomechanical constraints, temporal smoothness, postural balance, and physical plausibility.

Human-Scene Interaction (HSI) & Complex Motion Modeling

Dynamic Scene Understanding: Build and train custom architectures capable of handling extreme motion blur, severe self-occlusion, and multi-person crowding inherent in real-world human behavior.
Allocentric & Egocentric Tracking: Use your models to track human bodies through complex spaces, mapping foot-to-ground contact, joint torques, and environmental affordances to provide rich regularization for downstream action-conditioned robotics models (especially humanoid robots).

Emergent Perception R&D

Rapid Prototyping: Tackle novel, unmapped AI challenges as they arise. You will rapidly prototype and deploy new models for tasks spanning fine-grained action segmentation, intent prediction, and novel hardware sensor integrations.
Agile Problem Solving: Pivot to resolve sudden algorithmic bottlenecks in the data engine, adapting the latest research to unblock new product capabilities for our robotics customers.

Dense Contact & Physics-Aware Tracking

Interaction Integration: Connect the outputs of your foundational tracking models into highly optimized pipelines that reason about physical contact surfaces, gravity, and momentum, directly bridging the gap between human video data and robotic control/locomotion policies.

Who You Are

Required Background

Deep expertise in Deep Learning, 3D Computer Vision, and specifically Articulated Tracking / Human Body Pose Estimation.
Proven experience training large-scale vision models from scratch, not just running inference or fine-tuning existing checkpoints.
Strong theoretical and practical understanding of parametric human body models (e.g., SMPL, SMPL-X, GHUM, MHR, SOMA-X), inverse kinematics, and dense mesh estimation.
Mastery of PyTorch and deep learning scaling frameworks.
Experience handling and curating massive, multi-terabyte image and video datasets for training.
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities can shift rapidly to capitalize on new research or hardware capabilities.

Strong Signals:

First-author publications in top-tier venues (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS) focusing on 3D human pose tracking, human-scene interaction (HSI), human motion capture, or human mesh recovery.
Specific experience working with massive human motion and interaction datasets (e.g., AMASS, Human3.6M, EgoBody, PROX) and solving the unique optimization challenges they present.

Why This Role?

The Data Advantage: You will have access to a scale and quality of proprietary spatial and temporal ground truth for human motion that most academic researchers only dream of.
Pure R&D & Model Ownership: You are not maintaining legacy systems; you are given a blank slate and the compute resources to build the state-of-the-art.
High Impact: The kinematic priors and interaction models you architect will directly define how the next generation of embodied AI agents—from mobile manipulators to humanoid robots—learn to physically navigate, balance, and interact with the world.

Warning:
Research Scientist positions require hyper-specific expertise. Please limit your applications to one research role. Applying to multiple Research Scientist positions suggests a lack of focus and may result in the rejection of all submissions. You may, however, apply to other non-research roles alongside your research application.

A Note on Applying

Studies show women and candidates from underrepresented groups often only apply when they meet 100% of the listed qualifications, while others apply after meeting 60%. If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

Inclusive Hiring at Mecka

We are committed to creating an inclusive and supportive candidate experience. Should you require any accommodation whatsoever during the interview process, please inform us without any hesitation. Mecka is dedicated to ensuring equal treatment and opportunity in all phases of recruitment, selection, and employment, in compliance with employment law. We do not discriminate based on gender, race, religion, national origin, ethnicity, disability, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other protected category. Mecka is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, fostering a culture of inclusivity and maintaining a work environment that is free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

Use of Artificial Intelligence in Recruitment

Mecka uses artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly to support administrative and efficiency-focused aspects of our recruitment process. This includes activities such as drafting job descriptions, generating interview questions, note-taking and recordings, and supporting sourcing and scheduling workflows. All candidate evaluations, interviews, and hiring decisions are made by members of the Mecka team. While AI tools may assist with screening and assessment, they do not replace human judgment in selection decisions. Our use of AI is intended to streamline routine tasks, improve consistency, and enhance the overall candidate experience. We are committed to upholding principles of fairness, transparency, and accountability in all hiring activities. Mecka regularly reviews its recruitment practices to mitigate bias and to ensure alignment with applicable laws and evolving best practices.

About Us:

At ClarityPay, we’re redefining the point-of-sale credit market to bring more value to merchants. Based in NYC and Atlanta, our fast-growing fintech empowers large merchants with configurable “Pay-Over-Time” tools— including monthly installments, BNPL, and revolving products. Role Overview:

ClarityPay is seeking Forward Deployed Engineers to embed with the teams that run the company and turn how they work into dependable, AI-native systems. You will sit with process owners in finance, credit and portfolio risk, servicing and collections, and operations; scope the problem with them before building; ship agents, controls and automations into production; and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process. You will join the Data & AI organization, working alongside engineers in New York and India on a shared platform, and alongside Product and Engineering you will build external-facing AI solutions for merchants and partners on the ClarityPay platform. You will use AI tooling to make the build the easy part, and you will be measured on what is adopted and relied upon, not on what is demoed.

Key Responsibilities:

Embed with process owners to map how the work actually runs, scope the problem with them before building, and agree success criteria and a baseline up front.
Own delivery end to end — discovery, technical scoping, system design, build and production rollout — and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process.
Choose the simplest dependable solution: simplify or remove a step before automating it, then pick a scheduled job, a triggered job, or a bounded agent with a defined mandate, action set, escalation owner and pause conditions.
Write evaluations for everything you ship: prove the output is correct before a team depends on it, and re-check it as models, data and processes change.
Instrument what you build, and the processes around it, with detective (“day-zero”) controls — thresholds, exception inventories and alerting, each with an action path and a named owner — so a breach surfaces the same day, not at month-end.
Build external-facing AI solutions for merchants and partners with Product and Engineering; anything external ships through Engineering’s review and deployment standards.
Codify reusable patterns, evals and harness standards so the second deployment is faster than the first; prefer reusable capabilities over one agent per task, and bring field signal back to the platform roadmap.
Work inside ClarityPay’s controls for AI — evaluate before exposure, bound the exposure, keep a person at the gate — and propose where a human must review, where automation may act unattended, and what gets logged.
Own the value case: set impact hypotheses and baselines, measure before and after, and report to executives on business impact, total effort saved (including review and maintenance), control quality and reuse.
Continually promote and apply ClarityPay values; be a role model of trust and integrity.

What Success Looks Like in Your First 6–12 Months:

Desktop and spreadsheet-based reporting processes are inventoried, baselined and moved onto AI agentic systems running on governed data, with a person at the gate where judgment is needed.
Recurring performance reporting — portfolio, collections, servicing and finance — is produced by agents from governed metrics rather than manual pulls, on time and traceable to source.
Day-zero controls are live in your first processes, each with a threshold, an action path and a named owner, so breaches surface the same day.
The effort returned is measured against the baseline, net of review, exceptions and maintenance, and reported to executives.
At least one external-facing solution for merchants or partners is in production and adopted.
The patterns, evals and agent-harness standards you built are reused by the next deployment.

Qualifications:

Curious, energetic, positive, solution-oriented, collaborative, trusted.
2–5 years of software engineering or technical deployment experience that includes working directly with business users — in operations, business systems, solutions engineering, or technical consulting.
Production experience with LLMs: prompt engineering, agent or skill development, and evaluation. Things other people depend on, not demos.
Strong Python and SQL: you write and review production code and use AI-assisted development to move faster. Low-code and automation platforms (e.g., Retool, Zapier, n8n) are useful, not a substitute.
Data fluency in a lakehouse environment (e.g., Databricks, ClickHouse): pull answers out of governed data, build reliable pipelines, and catch when the output is wrong.
High agency and comfort with ambiguity — you will choose what to automate as often as you are told.
Strong discovery and communication skills: able to sit with a collections specialist or a finance analyst, understand their workflow, and explain trade-offs to a non-technical audience; comfortable working across time zones with engineering colleagues in India.
Judgment about what should not be automated — where the cost of being wrong outweighs the time saved.

Nice to Have:

Fintech, lending, payments, banking, or another regulated environment.
Experience building MCP servers, sub-agents, or agent skills.
MLOps or experimentation experience: evaluation frameworks, staged A/B tests, model monitoring.
Prior forward-deployed, professional services, or founding-engineer experience.

How You’ll Know This Role Is Right for You:

You see manual, repetitive work and cannot leave it alone.
You would rather ship a working automation this week than design the perfect one this quarter.

You want range: collections one month, month-end close the next, portfolio risk monitoring after that.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana

We're looking for a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead the AI behind Altana Nexus, our agentic platform for global trade. You'll work on a continuous stream of public and proprietary trade data (shipments, customs filings, trade documents), and build the models and AI agents that turn it into real-time decisions on risk, compliance and enforcement for governments and the world's largest companies.

Your Responsibilities

Drive the technical direction for agentic systems. Define the architecture and roadmap for the models and agentic systems that process trade data as it arrives (shipments, customs declarations, invoices, bills of lading) and turn it into risk, classification and compliance decisions in real time.
Build the pipeline from ingestion to decision. Lead the design of reliable, cost-efficient systems for ingestion, document understanding, entity resolution, inference and routing across models, at the scale of global trade.
Adapt models to trade. Use analyst feedback, production outcomes and agent traces to fine-tune and post-train models (SFT, DPO, RL with domain graders) where it measurably beats prompting, and keep every model improving over time.
Design the observability and feedback stack. Build the evals, tracing and feedback loops that decide what ships and catch regressions in production.
Lead beyond your team. Mentor senior engineers, raise the technical bar across Engineering, and help shape how we hire and level ML talent.
Shape the product and the business. Work with software engineers, data scientists, product managers and customers to generate new business ideas and turn ambiguous problems into shipped capabilities.

About You

BS/MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience
10+ years building and shipping ML systems in production, with a proven track record of delivering product-oriented ML solutions, including recent work on LLM-powered products
Deep expertise in PyTorch and the modern Python ML stack (Hugging Face, scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas/Polars)
Hands-on experience building production LLM applications: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool/function calling, structured outputs, and agentic workflows
You've shipped agentic systems in production and know their failure modes: tool use, planning, state, recovery and human-in-the-loop
Experience post-training or adapting LLMs (SFT, DPO, RLHF/RLAIF, reward modeling) for a production use case
Rigorous about evaluation: you've built eval suites, golden datasets and LLM-as-judge pipelines
Sound judgment on when to use a frontier model API, a fine-tuned open-weight model, or a classical ML model, balancing cost, latency, and accuracy
Senior Staff-level technical leadership: you set architecture direction across teams, mentor engineers, and turn ambiguous problems into roadmaps
Passionate about applying SOTA techniques to real-world problems, with a willingness to get your hands dirty in the data and domain to achieve measurable outcomes
You care deeply about engineering excellence, supportability and knowledge-sharing
You have strong written and verbal communication skills
Heavy user of AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) in your daily workflow

Nice To Have, But Not Required

Building multi-agent systems and agent tooling (e.g., LangGraph)
Hybrid retrieval: vector search, re-rankers, and embedding fine-tuning
Vision-language models for document understanding (invoices, bills of lading, customs forms)
Multilingual NLP
LLMOps: MLflow, Databricks Mosaic AI, and guardrails
Experience with safety, guardrails or auditability for AI in regulated or high-stakes domains (e.g., customs, legal, healthcare, finance)

Languages: Python, Spark
Tools: Docker, Git, Kubernetes, Swagger/OpenAPI, AWS, Azure
Datastores: Databricks, OpenSearch, Postgres
ML Tools: PyTorch, Hugging Face, FAISS, MLflow
LLM Tools: vLLM, LangGraph, LangSmith/Braintrust, frontier model APIs

This role is remote or hybrid, based in the United States, UK, with the option to work from one of our hubs in New York City, Boston, Washington D.C., or London

$250,000 - $295,000 USD

Benefits

The base salary offered to a successful candidate will depend on a wide range of compensation factors, including, but not limited to, work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Our Values

jobs.description:
About Mecka AI

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

We're looking for an experienced Research Scientist to advance the capabilities of large-scale vision-language and multimodal foundation models.

You'll work on challenging research problems spanning model training, post-training, reinforcement learning, and multimodal reasoning. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys experimenting with cutting-edge approaches, improving model performance, and translating research breakthroughs into real-world capabilities.

You'll have the opportunity to work across the model development lifecycle, from data and training strategies to evaluation and optimization, helping push the boundaries of what multimodal AI systems can understand and accomplish.

What You'll Do

Multimodal Model Research: Research, develop, and improve vision-language models and multimodal foundation-model architectures.
Post-Training & Reinforcement Learning: Design and implement advanced training strategies, including supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning, to improve model capabilities.
Model Performance & Optimization: Investigate approaches to improve reasoning, generalization, reliability, and training efficiency.
Data Quality & Training: Develop strategies for data curation, filtering, and synthetic data generation to improve training outcomes.
Evaluation & Benchmarking: Design experiments, evaluation frameworks, and benchmarks to measure model performance, identify failure modes, and guide research priorities.
Large-Scale Experimentation: Work with distributed training infrastructure and large-scale datasets to support research and model development.
Research Innovation: Explore emerging approaches in multimodal learning, model alignment, and foundation-model training.

What You Bring

Must Have

Hands-on experience researching, training, fine-tuning, or post-training large-scale foundation models, particularly vision-language or multimodal models.
Experience working with Qwen, Qwen-VL, or comparable open-weight multimodal foundation models.
Strong understanding of deep learning architectures, optimization techniques, and modern model training methodologies.
Practical experience with supervised fine-tuning (SFT), preference optimization, or reinforcement learning approaches such as DPO, GRPO, PPO, or RLHF.
Strong proficiency in Python and PyTorch, JAX, or comparable deep learning frameworks.
Experience designing, executing, and analyzing large-scale machine learning experiments.
Familiarity with distributed training systems and GPU-based model development.
Strong research instincts, analytical problem-solving skills, and the ability to independently drive complex technical projects.
Research publications, open-source contributions, or experience within leading AI research organizations.

Nice to Have

Experience with large-scale model post-training and reinforcement learning for reasoning or alignment.
Familiarity with multimodal data pipelines involving images, video, or other sensory inputs.
Experience with reward modeling, synthetic data generation, or advanced model evaluation.
Experience improving model capabilities through innovations in training strategies, data quality, or model architecture.

A Note on Applying

Studies show women and candidates from underrepresented groups often only apply when they meet 100% of the listed qualifications, while others apply after meeting 60%. If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

jobs.title: Applied AI Engineering Lead
jobs.description:
APPLIED AI ENGINEERING LEAD

Thresh Consulting — Strategy in Action for the AI Era

Salary: $190,000 – $235,000 + up to 25% performance-based bonus
Location: Hybrid (Denver, Chicago, or NYC preferred)

ABOUT THRESH

Thresh Consulting is a modern digital consulting firm built for the AI era—where strategy, execution, and craft come together to deliver real outcomes with speed. Our specialty is helping organizations design, build, and scale digital products that create exceptional customer experiences and drive value.

Our engineers are builders who work side by side with product & design. We value clarity over complexity, quality over shortcuts, and learning as a core part of growth.

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Applied AI Engineering Lead turns ambition into production systems that move a client's business. You'll own the technical direction of our AI engagements: deciding which problems are worth solving with AI, architecting the solution, and leading the team that ships it. Your depth is in applied LLM engineering: agents, tool use, retrieval, evaluation, and the guardrails that make AI safe to put in front of customers. You're fluent enough across front end, APIs, data, and cloud to build an experience end-to-end yourself when it counts.

You'll spend about 70% of your time building and 30% leading. You'll guide a team of 2-4 engineers and serve as a primary partner to client engineering leaders. You'll also work with Thresh's practice leads to scope and shape new AI work.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Set technical direction for AI engagements

Partner with clients to identify and prioritize high-value AI use cases, and be clear about what's ready for production versus what's still a demo.
Architect end-to-end LLM solutions: model selection, prompting strategy, retrieval, agents and tool use, and the integrations that connect them to real systems.
Make build, buy, prompt, or fine-tune calls based on cost, latency, quality, and risk, and explain those calls to client leadership.
Shape scope, estimates, and technical approach for new AI engagements alongside Thresh's practice and sales leads.

Build AI-powered, customer-facing experiences

Build conversational shopping experiences where customers discover, compare, and buy through natural language, from first question to completed order.
Set the patterns for streaming interfaces that stay fast and readable under real load, including partial responses, tool-call states, errors, and graceful fallbacks.
Bring real business logic into the conversation: live pricing, inventory, promotions, personalization, and customer account context.

Build agents, tools, and integrations

Build for a client's own site and app and for third-party AI assistants like ChatGPT and Gemini, all from one shared foundation.
Build and extend MCP servers and tools that give models safe, structured access to catalog, pricing, cart, and order capabilities.
Prepare commerce systems for AI agents that shop on a customer's behalf, with structured product data, agent-ready checkout, and clear rules for what an agent can and can't do.
Work with emerging agentic commerce protocols (ACP, UCP), and know where each fits a client's business model.
Integrate with enterprise commerce, catalog, order, and identity systems that were never designed for AI.
Design multi-step agents and workflows that take real actions in client systems, with clear permissions, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and audit trails.
Build retrieval and knowledge systems (RAG) over client content, catalogs, and documentation, and tune them for accuracy.

Make AI trustworthy in production

Build guardrails that keep the assistant in scope. That means no fabricated prices, promises, or commitments, and a clean handoff to a person or standard flow when a request goes past what it should handle.
Own the evaluation strategy. Build eval sets and automated test harnesses covering clean queries, edge cases, out-of-scope requests, and prompt-injection attempts, and turn what you find into fixes and release gates.
Instrument conversations end to end for analytics, attribution, observability, cost, and latency, so clients can measure what the experience drives.
Prepare work for the legal, privacy, security, and brand reviews that every transactional AI experience goes through.
Monitor model quality, drift, and spend after launch, and plan for model upgrades and vendor changes without breaking the experience.

Champion Agentic Development

Make AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor) your default way of working.
Write specs precise enough for an agent to implement against, then verify the output against the spec rather than the diff.
Prototype conversational features in days with mock data, so clients can see the experience before the real integrations land.
Test new tools and workflows, and bring what works back to the team and to the wider Thresh practice.

Lead and elevate

Mentor engineers through code review, pairing, and technical guidance, across the full applied AI stack, from prompting and evals to production architecture.
Partner with product managers and designers on conversation design, scope, technical risk, and estimates.
Define the components, patterns, and standards that become reusable assets across Thresh's AI work, including reference architectures and starter kits.
Help build Thresh's applied AI capability through hiring input, technical interviews, and internal enablement.
Represent Thresh's AI point of view with clients and platform partners through workshops, technical content, and pre-sales conversations.

Deliver for clients

Own AI solutions from discovery through production deployment.
Explain progress and tradeoffs clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including what AI can and can't reliably do.
Work within each client's existing stack, frameworks, and constraints.
Hold the quality bar when deadlines tighten and requirements shift.

WHAT YOU BRING

Technical

7+ years building and shipping production software, including 2+ years shipping LLM-powered products to real users.
Strong working knowledge of React, TypeScript, and Next.js enough to build, review, and guide production UI work.
Shipped streaming or conversational UI in production, including tool-calling patterns and structured model output.
Experience building or consuming MCP servers, or a comparable tool-integration layer for LLMs.
Deep, hands-on experience with LLM APIs and agent frameworks (e.g., Claude, OpenAI, Gemini; agent SDKs, LangGraph, or similar), including prompting, tool use, structured output, and multi-step agents.
Built retrieval-augmented systems in production, including embeddings, chunking, vector or hybrid search, and accuracy tuning.
Designed and run LLM evaluation frameworks, and used the results to make shipping decisions.
Practical understanding of LLM security and risk: prompt injection, data leakage, PII handling, and responsible AI practices.
Can reason about model cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs, and make model selection calls that hold up.
Strong back-end skills in Python and/or Node.js. You can design and build the services and APIs your AI systems need.
API experience across REST and/or GraphQL, plus working fluency with PostgreSQL and NoSQL stores.
Working knowledge of cloud platforms and their AI services (e.g., AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI), CI/CD, and Docker.
Daily, hands-on use of AI coding agents in real work. Be ready to show us how you use them.
Bonus: e-commerce, checkout, or payments experience in a high-volume environment.
Bonus: fine-tuning, classical ML, or data engineering experience for when a problem calls for it.

How you work

You ship production systems on time and at a high standard.
You do well when requirements evolve and priorities shift.
You debug across layers, propose fixes, and make pragmatic tradeoffs.
You know when "good enough" is the right call and when to push for excellence.
You care about the details users notice, and the ones they don't.
You've led technical teams through delivery and helped other engineers grow
You explain technical concepts to non-engineers clearly.
You can tell a client when AI isn't the right answer, and explain why.
Client-facing or professional services experience is strongly preferred.

WHY THRESH

Senior-level competitive compensation with performance bonus upside.
Comprehensive healthcare benefits.
401(k) with company matching.
High ownership and influence over technical direction of Thresh's AI practice.
Hybrid delivery flexibility with client travel and team co-locations.
A low-ego culture built on clarity, craft, and outcomes.

AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

jobs.title: Principal AI Product Engineer
jobs.description:
About Nscale

Nscale is taking on the hyperscalers by building a vertically integrated GenAI cloud platform. We own the data centers, software, and applications that power today's AI stack using sustainable technology solutions. We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As a Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Collaboration is key, and we work together swiftly and respectfully, embracing adaptability and resilience in all we do.

About The Role

Nscale is looking for a Principal AI Engineer (Specialised)
to lead the inference and post-training pillar of our AI systems engineering organization. You’ll define the multi-year technical roadmap for how models are served, evaluated, and post-trained on Nscale’s GPU cloud, across dedicated and serverless inference and bring-your-own-model deployments. You’ll lead the most consequential architectural programmes in that space and set the engineering standards that 20–50+ engineers build to.

As a Principal engineer, you are one of the deepest technical authorities in the company on AI systems. Your decisions set the cost, latency, and reliability at which Nscale serves tokens and runs post-training workloads, and those numbers have to compete with the world’s leading AI infrastructure providers. The problems span the full stack: kernel efficiency on state-of-the-art GPU systems, fleet-level KV cache and serving architecture, the evals that prove model quality, and RL loops where inference and training share hardware. You frame the solutions the organization executes against, including the API contracts customers see.

How We Work

Dog years. We move quickly and compress a lot of learning into a short time.
Don’t let perfect be the enemy of good. Ship, measure, iterate.
Be relentless. Own the problem end to end and see it through.
One team, one mission. Outcomes over process, and no “not my job”.

Responsibilities

Define and own the multi-year technical roadmap for Nscale’s inference, evals, and post-training platform, and translate it into architecture that multiple teams can execute against
Lead company-scale architectural initiatives in the pillar, such as next-generation serving (disaggregated prefill/decode, KV cache orchestration across GPU, host, and storage tiers, speculative decoding, multi-tenant scheduling), GPU kernel and model efficiency work (custom kernels, FP8/NVFP4/INT8/4 quantization, sparsity, distillation, MoE serving), evals and benchmarking frameworks, and post-training and RL infrastructure
Establish engineering standards adopted across all AI teams: API design and compatibility guarantees, benchmarking and evals methodology, training stability norms, and performance testing practices
Own the framework by which cost, latency, throughput, and model quality trade-offs are made and measured across the pillar
Identify long-horizon systemic risks early (serving engine and framework bets, accelerator support, capability gaps) and resolve them before they block the organization
Align AI engineering, research, product, and infrastructure leadership on multi-team technical strategy; frame technical trade-offs in product and commercial terms
Mentor and develop Staff and Senior AI Engineers, and grow the next generation of inference technical leaders at Nscale
Represent Nscale’s technical approach externally: open-source leadership in the frameworks we depend on, publications, conference talks, and partnerships with GPU vendors and AI labs

jobs.title: Specialist Solutions Architect, Radar (Fraud/Risk)
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSA) are domain experts aligned to specific Stripe solutions and customer buying centers. We have in-depth knowledge of specific solution offerings and understanding of customers' challenges. We advise the broader pre-sales team on complex opportunities, support pipeline development and revenue attainment, serve as an advisor on go-to-market sales plays, and provide critical insights to our product and engineering teams.

Stripe Radar is Stripe's fully integrated fraud and risk management platform. The Radar team's mission is to evolve from a best-in-class payment fraud product into a unified risk intelligence platform that protects businesses from all forms of financial loss—from sophisticated payment fraud and account takeovers to first-party misuse and policy abuse. With Radar, businesses can confidently navigate the evolving fraud landscape, accept more good revenue, and focus on growth.

What you'll do

You'll collaborate closely with sales and pre-sales teams to drive pipeline and revenue targets, while also educating the product and engineering teams on market trends and influencing the product roadmap. You'll develop deep relationships with senior customer business leaders and grow Stripe's solution offerings with new and existing customers. As subject matter experts, you'll scale the broader organization by creating reusable assets and coaching others on complex high-value opportunities. You'll also run customer workshops and take the lead on key opportunities. You'll serve as the domain and product expert to our users and GTM team for Stripe Radar globally.

Responsibilities

Act as a subject matter expert on Stripe's Radar product suite to accelerate opportunities globally.
Demonstrate a deep understanding and point of view on trends in the fraud and risk management ecosystem, including AI-powered detection, processor-agnostic architectures, and the shift from payment fraud to holistic business risk (e.g., policy abuse, account takeover, first-party misuse).
Develop expertise with the functional and architectural patterns for deploying advanced fraud systems, including the lifecycle of rule management, ML model tuning, and manual review optimization.
Understand the ecosystem of risk and identity integrations (e.g., device fingerprinting, identity verification, bot mitigation, case management) Stripe must support for our users to be successful.
Define, share, and learn best practices and reusable assets with the broader GTM organization to enhance the quality and efficiency of the team.
Create reference architectures to uplevel the team and refine reference solutions based on product enhancements and feedback from customers.
Partner closely with the Radar product sales team and be an active part of the opportunity team for Stripe's largest and most complex Radar customers to lead strategy and own key customer relationships.
Partner closely with the Radar product team to get early exposure to the new products and features.
Serve as a "Voice of the Customer" internally to drive product and feature request prioritization, providing actionable insights on the competitive landscape and emerging fraud vectors.
Act as an escalation point to drive our most complex technical issues to resolution with Stripe's engineering team.
Support customers and Stripe teammates on account or deal strategy, and answer product feature and technical questions.
Understand the sales process for the product and provide the Sales team with tools and training to qualify potential leads.
Stay current on competitive analysis and market differentiation.
Support marketing events including executive briefings, conferences, user groups, and trade shows.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of experience in a pre-sales, technical consulting, product, or risk strategy role focused on e-commerce fraud prevention, risk management, or trust and safety
Deep working knowledge of the fraud and risk ecosystem, including payment fraud (CNP), account takeover (ATO), first-party misuse (friendly fraud), and policy and content abuse
Demonstrated knowledge of risk management architectures, including the role of rules engines, machine learning models, and manual review queues in fraud decisioning
Strong knowledge of the signals and data used in fraud detection, such as device and IP data, behavioral biometrics, identity verification, and graph-based analysis
Strong knowledge of software engineering and architecture patterns, with the ability to understand how a wide variety of technologies and systems interact with each other
Outstanding communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, comfortable explaining complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
Interest in solving open-ended business problems with a combination of technology and creative thinking
A proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with business partners
Ability to deal effectively with ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment

Preferred Qualifications

Experience integrating Stripe or other RESTful APIs into web applications
Experience with processor-agnostic fraud solutions and multi-processor payment environments
Experience with risk management for various business models, such as platforms and marketplaces, subscription services, and digital goods and SaaS
Familiarity with liability shift programs (e.g., chargeback guarantees) and value-based pricing models for risk products
Understanding of how to extend fraud protection beyond payments to other products like payouts (Issuing), physical payments (Terminal), or recurring billing (Billing)
Experience as a subject matter expert in a relevant industry, vertical, or product

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $184,900 - $277,300. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana

We're looking for a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead the AI behind Altana Nexus, our agentic platform for global trade. You'll work on a continuous stream of public and proprietary trade data (shipments, customs filings, trade documents), and build the models and AI agents that turn it into real-time decisions on risk, compliance and enforcement for governments and the world's largest companies.

Your Responsibilities

Drive the technical direction for agentic systems. Define the architecture and roadmap for the models and agentic systems that process trade data as it arrives (shipments, customs declarations, invoices, bills of lading) and turn it into risk, classification and compliance decisions in real time.
Build the pipeline from ingestion to decision. Lead the design of reliable, cost-efficient systems for ingestion, document understanding, entity resolution, inference and routing across models, at the scale of global trade.
Adapt models to trade. Use analyst feedback, production outcomes and agent traces to fine-tune and post-train models (SFT, DPO, RL with domain graders) where it measurably beats prompting, and keep every model improving over time.
Design the observability and feedback stack. Build the evals, tracing and feedback loops that decide what ships and catch regressions in production.
Lead beyond your team. Mentor senior engineers, raise the technical bar across Engineering, and help shape how we hire and level ML talent.
Shape the product and the business. Work with software engineers, data scientists, product managers and customers to generate new business ideas and turn ambiguous problems into shipped capabilities.

About You

BS/MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience
8+ years building and shipping ML systems in production, with a proven track record of delivering product-oriented ML solutions, including recent work on LLM-powered products
Deep expertise in PyTorch and the modern Python ML stack (Hugging Face, scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas/Polars)
Hands-on experience building production LLM applications: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool/function calling, structured outputs, and agentic workflows
You've shipped agentic systems in production and know their failure modes: tool use, planning, state, recovery and human-in-the-loop
Experience post-training or adapting LLMs (SFT, DPO, RLHF/RLAIF, reward modeling) for a production use case
Rigorous about evaluation: you've built eval suites, golden datasets and LLM-as-judge pipelines
Sound judgment on when to use a frontier model API, a fine-tuned open-weight model, or a classical ML model, balancing cost, latency, and accuracy
Passionate about applying SOTA techniques to real-world problems, with a willingness to get your hands dirty in the data and domain to achieve measurable outcomes
You care deeply about engineering excellence, supportability and knowledge-sharing
You have strong written and verbal communication skills
Heavy user of AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) in your daily workflow

Nice To Have, But Not Required

Building multi-agent systems and agent tooling (e.g., LangGraph)
Hybrid retrieval: vector search, re-rankers, and embedding fine-tuning
Vision-language models for document understanding (invoices, bills of lading, customs forms)
Multilingual NLP
LLMOps: MLflow, Databricks Mosaic AI, and guardrails
Experience with safety, guardrails or auditability for AI in regulated or high-stakes domains (e.g., customs, legal, healthcare, finance)

Technologies we love

Languages: Python, Spark
Tools: Docker, Git, Kubernetes, Swagger/OpenAPI, AWS, Azure
Datastores: Databricks, OpenSearch, Postgres
ML Tools: PyTorch, Hugging Face, FAISS, MLflow
LLM Tools: vLLM, LangGraph, LangSmith/Braintrust, frontier model APIs

This role is remote or hybrid, based in the United States, UK, with the option to work from one of our hubs in New York City, Boston, Washington D.C., or London

$205,000 - $240,000 USD

There is also a Flexible Spending Account (FSA) option.

Our values are the core beliefs that shape who we are, what we stand for, and how we behave.They form the foundation of Altana’s culture and integrity and guide how we hire, design, build, and connect with each other and our customers.

Trust: Our customers and partners entrust us with missions of the highest importance. We honor that by keeping our word, meeting commitments, and ensuring every action we take reinforces confidence in us. We rely on each other to deliver, to speak openly, and to hold ourselves accountable.

Job Description

As an AI Solutions Architect
, you will help law firm customers transform how legal work gets done with Thomson Reuters Legal AI. Combining legal-practice experience, product expertise, and a practical understanding of AI, you will identify high-value legal workflows, design and test AI-enabled solutions, and help customers move successful use cases into sustained adoption. Working closely with Customer Success Managers, you will support adoption across customer organizations, with a particular focus on enabling high-value users and scaling successful workflows.

Key Responsibilities

In the role of AI Solutions Architect,
you will collaborate closely with Customer Success, Sales, and Product teams to:

Lead in-person discovery sessions, solution demonstrations, workflow workshops, and executive briefings with law firm customers to identify priority legal workflows and show how Thomson Reuters Legal AI can address them.
Support customers throughout the lifecycle by identifying and prioritizing Legal AI use cases, advising on workflow and solution design, demonstrating relevant capabilities, and helping successful use cases scale across teams and practice areas.
Partner closely with Customer Success Managers to develop and execute Legal AI adoption strategies for a portfolio of select law firm customers, with particular emphasis on enabling high-value users, expanding successful workflows, and supporting sustained product usage.
Discover, test, and document best practices for applying Thomson Reuters Legal AI across customer workflows, creating reusable use cases, prompts, playbooks, and workflow patterns that can scale.
Apply a strong understanding of the legal technology ecosystem to determine when customer needs are best addressed through Thomson Reuters products, a partner solution, an integration, or custom development, and bring together the appropriate technical and business partners.
Support customer advocacy by communicating customer needs to Customer Success and our cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, and Marketing, and highlighting opportunities to improve and innovate our legal AI products.
Contribute to Thomson Reuters’ thought leadership by sharing expertise with customers and the broader market through events, advisory boards, or customer-facing content.
Be an effective advocate for Thomson Reuters products. Understand their strengths, areas for improvement, and roadmaps, and be able to explain on multiple levels how they can be specifically applied to take customers’ client advocacy to new heights.
Travel: This role requires regular travel (approximately 25-30%, varying by quarter) to customer and firm sites to support client engagements, demonstrations, and team initiatives. Candidates must be willing and able to travel as a condition of employment.

You are a fit for the role of AI Solutions Architect
if you have the following required qualifications:

J.D. from an accredited US law school required.
Prior experience practicing law required (e.g., in a law firm, in-house legal department, government, clerkship, or comparable legal practice setting).
Proven experience in customer- or client-facing roles, ideally engaging with Enterprise or complex accounts.
Familiarity with legal workflows and processes such as due diligence, eDiscovery, large document review, compliance, or related domains — gained through direct practice, adjacent roles, or working with legal professionals.
Demonstrable experience with generative artificial intelligence applications.
Substantial experience using a variety of online legal research and practice tools (e.g. Westlaw, Practical Law, HighQ, Relativity, Everlaw, etc.).
Tech-savvy with a strong aptitude for learning new AI tools and platforms; no formal technical or programming background is required.
Experience with basic programming (Python) and/or exploratory coding for problem-solving is a plus but not required.
Bring experience in customer-facing roles, ideally working with Enterprise accounts.
Understand the architecture and operation of large language models (LLMs) and are comfortable working hands-on with AI tools, even without a formal technical or engineering background.
Approach challenges constructively, framing Thomson Reuters solutions positively and accurately.
Are knowledgeable in due diligence, eDiscovery, managing large document sets, data rooms, and related workflows where AI can accelerate results.
Excel at communicating technical concepts and creating clear, high-quality documentation and learning materials, and can craft persuasive presentations that resonate with non-technical and often skeptical customers by focusing on their needs and outcomes rather than just product features.
Thrive on working directly with motivated customers to solve complex problems, including through in-person, on-site engagements.
Bring creativity, curiosity, and a growth mindset to problem-solving, with the ability to simplify ambiguous challenges and turn them into opportunities.
Stay up-to-date with emerging AI research and industry trends, and think critically about risks, opportunities, and societal impact.
Embrace innovation and experimentation—you view setbacks as opportunities to learn, iterate, and improve outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

Bring experience in customer-facing roles, ideally working with Enterprise accounts.

Approach challenges constructively, framing Thomson Reuters solutions positively and accurately.

Thrive on working directly with motivated customers to solve complex problems, including through in-person, on-site engagements.
Bring creativity, curiosity, and a growth mindset to problem-solving, with the ability to simplify ambiguous challenges and turn them into opportunities.
Stay up-to-date with emerging AI research and industry trends, and think critically about risks, opportunities, and societal impact.
Embrace innovation and experimentation—you view setbacks as opportunities to learn, iterate, and improve outcomes.

What’s in it For You?

Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.

jobs.title: Staff ML Engineer, Generative Model Performance & Efficiency
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Simulator Team at Waymo builds state-of-the-art simulations of realistic environments for testing, training, and validation of the Waymo Driver. Our team is a diverse, and collaborative group of machine learning (ML) engineers, software engineers, and ML research engineers. We develop industry-leading simulation solutions using advanced generative and reconstructive ML algorithms, to model the real world, encompassing realistic agents, roads, traffic systems, weather, and the full sensor suite (Camera, Lidar, Radar).

To accelerate the fidelity, scalability, controllability, and richness of our simulations, we are pushing the frontiers of 3D world modeling. We leverage state-of-the-art ML technologies trained on large-scale datasets to create dynamic and semantically rich virtual worlds, directly impacting the development and validation of the Waymo Driver.

In this role, you will report to a Senior Staff Engineering Manager

You Will

Analyze model architectures and identify bottlenecks in training and inference performance (e.g., memory bandwidth, compute, communication).
Apply and develop techniques such as quantization (e.g., FP8, INT4), pruning, knowledge distillation, and efficient attention mechanisms.
Optimize model code for specific hardware accelerators (TPUs, GPUs), leveraging compiler features and low-level libraries (e.g., XLA).
Experiment with different model partitioning and sharding strategies (e.g., data, tensor, pipeline parallelism, expert parallelism) to improve scalability and efficiency.
Design and implement low-latency, high-throughput serving solutions for generative models and optimize training pipelines to reduce training time.
Build and maintain tools for performance analysis, profiling (e.g., xprof), and debugging of ML models.

You Have

MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related field.
5+ years of experience with deep learning architectures (especially Transformers, Diffusion Models, MoEs), algorithms, and optimization techniques.
Proficiency in JAX, Flax, and potentially TensorFlow/PyTorch.
Expertise in using profiling tools (e.g., XProf, Perfetto, NVIDIA Nsight) to diagnose performance issues in ML workloads.
Hands-on experience with quantization, pruning, distillation, and other model compression methods.
Strong programming skills in Python and potentially C++, with experience in software development best practices.

We Prefer

Knowledge of TPU and GPU architectures and how to optimize code for them.
Familiarity with ML compilers like XLA and an understanding of how they translate high-level code to efficient hardware instructions.
Understanding of concepts related to training and serving models across multiple devices and machines.
Experience contributing to frameworks and libraries that improve training speed and scalability (e.g., JAX, Gemax, XManager).

Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level.
