new_jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer-Voice AI Agent Prompting
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Forward Deployed Engineer, Voice AI Agent Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates voice AI agents whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret caller intent over a live audio channel, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the caller's behalf. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: shaping ambiguous call flows and telephony requirements into precise specifications, authoring the instructions and prompts that govern voice agent behavior, proving through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly on real calls. This is not a machine learning or AI research role — the engineer does not train foundation or speech models — but it is distinct from traditional software engineering, where systems follow deterministic call-flow logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime.

Two things follow, and voice makes both harder. First, the agent's most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, and guardrails — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, while also holding up under what a spoken channel adds: turn-taking, barge-in, and disambiguating what speech recognition got wrong. Second, because behavior is probabilistic and happens live on a call, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale — including latency, containment, and transcription accuracy — rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first-class engineering activity rather than a quality-assurance afterthought. The engineer owns the correctness of what ships to a live caller, whether a human or an agent produced it.

What You Get To Do In This Role

Build voice AI agents. Design and ship agentic voice applications — intent interpretation, multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the caller's behalf — together with the CTI, CCaaS, and telephony integrations that make them usable in production.
Design AI-driven autonomous voice workflows. Decompose call flows and business processes into the steps and decision points a voice agent can execute — determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a live-agent handoff is required, and how misrecognition, retries, and escalation are handled.
Engineer for what voice demands. Build experiences that hold context across turns, manage barge-in and interruption, recover gracefully from speech-recognition error, disambiguate caller intent, and confirm before consequential actions — all within the latency budget a live call imposes.
Author and maintain voice agent instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern voice agent behavior — as engineering artifacts under review and regression coverage, not configuration text.
Engineer prompts for reliability rather than demo quality. Iterate prompts against measured call outcomes: task decomposition, golden call transcripts, structured output schemas, grounding and citation, graceful hand-back to a human agent, and the token and latency cost that directly shapes caller experience.
Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic voice behavior. Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe on a live channel — golden call datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring calibrated to human QA review, CI gates, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool-selection testing specific to voice.
Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert customer call-flow and telephony requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it.
Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the voice stack. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — building against their call data, integrations, and channels, tuning instructions and evaluation sets against live traffic, and returning with evidence that improves the product.
Own quality, safety, and reliability on live calls. Monitor call containment, hallucination, unsafe actions, and transcription accuracy; defend against prompt injection and data leakage on live calls; and feed production call failures back into specifications and evaluation sets.
Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers and platform teams to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly

Qualifications

To Be Successful in This Role:

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production voice applications, including hands-on delivery of AI-native voice agent features that real callers depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts for voice, designing AI-driven autonomous call workflows, and building the evaluation and testing that verifies them against live call traffic, is required. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their voice and contact center environment, is required. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice AI agents.

Key Competencies, Skills, And Experience

Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing.
AI native voice application development. Hands-on experience building applications where model-driven behavior is central — agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling the latency, cost, and failure modes unique to a live audio channel.
AI-driven autonomous workflow design. Demonstrated experience designing workflows in which voice agents carry out multi-step call processes with limited supervision: call-flow decomposition, decision points and autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception and retry handling, and observability over what the agent did and why.
Voice and telephony platform expertise. Practical experience with telephony integration, speech recognition and synthesis, and streaming audio — including the barge-in, turn-taking, and confirmation patterns a live call requires.
Agentic instruction authoring. Demonstrated skill writing and maintaining the natural-language logic that governs voice agent behavior — instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and refusal and escalation rules — with versioning, review, and regression coverage applied as they would be to code.
Prompt engineering. Intent-driven prompt design tuned for voice: decomposition, golden and few-shot examples, structured output and schema enforcement, grounding and citation, and disciplined iteration against call-level evaluation results rather than impressions.
Evaluation and testing of non-deterministic voice systems. Ability to build measurable frameworks assessing call quality, agent behavior, tool-selection accuracy, and regression risk — golden call datasets, scenario suites, model-as-judge scoring with human QA calibration, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, and grounding testing.
Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define call-flow problems rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements them correctly, and to decide soundly when to solve a problem in code, in instructions, or by delegating to an agent.
Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated voice applications — prompt injection, sensitive-data and call-recording leakage, over-broad tool access, unsafe autonomous action — translated into concrete guardrails, least-privilege controls, and monitoring.
Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers.

Desired Experience

Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.
Voice and contact center technology. Telephony and contact center platforms, IVR, speech recognition and synthesis, streaming audio, and real-time latency optimization.
Conversation design partnership. Experience working alongside conversation or content designers, contributing to dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design.
Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production call transcripts at scale.
Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, sales, or enterprise workflow, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.
Years of Experience. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers

🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!

Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops.

As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact.

We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce.

💻 Role

The Seller Merchant team helps sellers bring inventory onto Whatnot, organize it effectively, and make it easier to sell. That includes products, listings, variants, catalog, taxonomy, inventory creation, seller workflows, and integrations such as Shopify.

Our sellers range from someone going live for the first time on their phone to sophisticated merchants managing large inventories across multiple systems. They also operate across very different categories, countries, and selling formats. The right product experience for one seller may be completely wrong for another.

As a Data Scientist on Seller Merchant, you'll use data to help us understand those differences and build better products for sellers. Your work will ultimately help sellers become more productive, grow their businesses, and bring more high-quality supply to the marketplace.

You'll

Identify and prioritize the highest-impact opportunities to improve seller success. Use product analysis, opportunity sizing, and strategic thinking to understand where changes to seller workflows can have the largest impact on activation, inventory creation, selling efficiency, and GMV.
Design and evaluate experiments across the seller experience. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design to turn ambiguous questions into testable hypotheses, define success metrics and guardrails, design rigorous experiments, and translate results into product decisions.
Develop the analytical frameworks that shape product strategy. Go beyond answering incoming questions by proactively identifying opportunities, defining new ways to measure seller success, and helping the team decide what to build next.
Understand how different sellers need different products. Analyze differences across seller size, maturity, category, country, inventory type, and selling format, and help determine when a single experience works versus when we should build for distinct seller segments.
Help us make good decisions even when the data isn't perfect. Supply-side problems often involve smaller samples, heterogeneous populations, or decisions where data provides important evidence without giving a black-and-white answer. You'll apply analytics, causal inference, and other statistical approaches where appropriate, while partnering closely with product leaders to combine evidence with sound judgment.

You'll be deeply embedded with the product team, but you'll also have meaningful independence to develop your own hypotheses, challenge existing thinking, and use data to influence where the team invests.

We offer flexibility to work from home or from one of our global office hubs, and we value in-person time for planning, problem-solving, and connection. Team members in this role must live within commuting distance of our New York, San Francisco hub.

👋 You

People who do well at Whatnot tend to be comfortable figuring things out as they go, biased toward action, and genuinely curious about what they're building. They care more about outcomes than credit and stay close to the product and the people using it.

As Our Next Data Scientist, You Should Have 5+ Years Of Experience In Product Data Science, Analytics, Or a Closely Related Field, Plus

A Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Mathematics, a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant technical training.
Strong product and business judgment, with experience translating ambiguous product questions into hypotheses, analyses, experiments, and recommendations.
Deep knowledge of experimentation, causal inference, and statistical methods, including approaches appropriate for smaller or noisier datasets such as Bayesian methods.
Strong statistical judgment: you understand what the data can support, what it can't, and when additional product or business judgment is required.
Advanced SQL skills and working proficiency in Python. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable using code to investigate data, perform statistical analysis, and evaluate or debug AI-assisted work.
Experience working closely with Product and Engineering teams and influencing decisions rather than simply delivering analysis.
The ability to disagree constructively: you can push back when the evidence warrants it, communicate uncertainty clearly, and maintain strong working relationships with cross-functional partners.
A track record of independently identifying opportunities and driving analytical work from problem framing through recommendation and impact.

Experience with e-commerce, merchant products, inventory systems, seller tools, or two-sided marketplaces is a plus, but not required.

Bonus signals we look for

You've questioned an existing approach and built something better rather than copying what was done before.
You've owned outcomes end-to-end, not just tasks within a narrow scope.
You've stepped outside your job description to solve a problem because it needed to get done.
You use Whatnot as a buyer or seller and can speak to the product with real context.
You've worked on a marketplace, platform, or product where meaningfully different user groups required different product experiences or analytical approaches.
You've made consequential product recommendations in situations where the data was incomplete, ambiguous, or statistically challenging.

What You'll Get at Whatnot

Compressed career growth. Short feedback loops, real ownership, and problems no one has solved before mean you learn faster. People regularly say one year here equals three elsewhere, and high performers take on more responsibility quickly.
Category-defining work. Live commerce at this scale has never been done in the West. Your work shapes how an entirely new industry develops.
Exceptional colleagues. We're deliberate about talent density. Your coworkers will challenge your thinking, raise your standards, and make you better.
Real ownership. You'll be expected to form opinions, influence decisions, and own outcomes - not just execute a queue of analytical requests.
Tangible seller impact. Sellers are the supply side of our marketplace and are building real businesses on Whatnot. Helping them onboard, operate more efficiently, and grow is fundamental to the company's growth.
Intellectually difficult problems. Seller data is often heterogeneous, sparse, and deeply tied to real-world business behavior. The interesting questions rarely reduce to a single metric or obvious experiment.
AI-forward tools and workflows. We invest in modern AI tools and expect them to be part of daily work. The important skill is increasingly not just writing code, but knowing what questions to ask, moving quickly, and recognizing when the output is, or isn't, trustworthy.
Rewarding collaboration. The work is challenging, but the people are great and wins get celebrated.

🎁 Benefits

Generous Holiday and Time off Policy
Health Insurance options including Medical, Dental, Vision
Work From Home Support
Home office setup allowance
Monthly allowance for cell phone and internet

Care benefits
Monthly allowance for wellness
Annual allowance towards Childcare

Retirement; 401k offering for Traditional and Roth accounts in the US (employer match up to 4% of base salary) and Pension plans internationally

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, ML Infrastructure (MDX)
new_jobs.description:
About The Team

DoorDash's MDX team sits within Machine Learning Platform and builds the shared foundation that ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo rely on to build and run ML-powered products. We work across the full ML lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment, serving, and monitoring. Our mission is to increase the velocity and reliability of ML-driven business impact across the company. A central pillar of that work is agentic infrastructure. We are building systems that let agents accelerate and operate the ML workflow itself, including auto research, where agents explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and self-healing systems that detect, diagnose, and remediate failures in ML pipelines and production models with minimal human intervention.

About The Role

You will join a small, high-leverage team building the agentic layer of DoorDash's ML infrastructure. You'll design and build the systems that let agents accelerate how ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo develop, ship, and operate models. That includes auto research systems that explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and agentic developer support that helps ML engineers move through training, evaluation, deployment, and debugging faster. You'll own well-scoped components end to end, from design through production, working across agent orchestration, tooling and integrations with our ML platform, evaluation of agent behavior, and observability. This role is ideal for an engineer with a strong backend foundation who is excited to apply AI agents to real engineering workflows, learns quickly, and wants to grow into technical leadership in a fast-moving area where model capabilities, tooling, and best practices change month to month.

You're Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…

Build agentic systems that increase the velocity of ML development across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, helping ML engineers get from idea to production model faster.
Design and implement infrastructure that lets agents propose, run, and evaluate modeling experiments.
Build agentic developer support for the ML lifecycle, such as agents that help engineers set up training jobs, debug failing pipelines, review model deployments, and navigate our platform.
Develop evaluation and observability for agent behavior, so we can measure whether agents are actually helping, catch regressions early, and build the trust needed to give them more autonomy.
Work with production standards in mind, including reliability, safety guardrails, cost controls, monitoring, and clear playbooks, so that agentic workflows can run against real ML systems.
Partner closely with ML engineers, data scientists, and platform teams to understand where their time goes and turn those workflows into durable, reusable platform capabilities.
Grow quickly in a fast-moving area, with the chance to shape how agents are used to build and operate ML systems at a company of this scale.

We're Excited About You Because…

B.S., M.S., or PhD in Computer Science or equivalent
2+ years of industry experience in software engineering
Hands-on experience building ML infrastructure in production including feature engineering and feature stores, data pipelines for ML, training and experimentation platforms, model evaluation, deployment, serving and inference, or monitoring
Strong backend engineering fundamentals, especially in Python and distributed systems
Experience operating systems in production, including testing, observability, debugging, and reliability
A good understanding of how ML engineers and data scientists work, and a track record of building platforms, tools, or services that make them more productive
Ability to take ambiguous, well-scoped problems from idea to production, and to learn quickly in a fast-moving technical area
Proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) across the software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring, and releasing software

Nice To Haves

Experience building LLM-powered applications or AI agents, including tool use, orchestration, or MCP servers, in production or on substantial projects
Experience with agent evaluation, LLM observability, tracing, or building eval harnesses
Experience with ML platforms or MLOps tooling (e.g., Kubeflow, MLflow, Ray, Airflow)
Experience with Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP)
Experience building developer tools, internal platforms, or self-serve infrastructure
Experience with guardrails, safety, or cost controls for LLM systems

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. new_jobs.description:
About The Team

DoorDash's MDX team sits within Machine Learning Platform and builds the shared foundation that ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo rely on to build and run ML-powered products. We work across the full ML lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment, serving, and monitoring. Our mission is to increase the velocity and reliability of ML-driven business impact across the company. A central pillar of that work is agentic infrastructure. We are building systems that let agents accelerate and operate the ML workflow itself, including auto research, where agents explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and self-healing systems that detect, diagnose, and remediate failures in ML pipelines and production models with minimal human intervention.

About The Role

You will join a small, high-leverage team building the agentic layer of DoorDash's ML infrastructure. You'll design and build the systems that let agents accelerate how ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo develop, ship, and operate models. That includes auto research systems that explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and agentic developer support that helps ML engineers move through training, evaluation, deployment, and debugging faster. You'll own well-scoped components end to end, from design through production, working across agent orchestration, tooling and integrations with our ML platform, evaluation of agent behavior, and observability. This role is ideal for an engineer with a strong backend foundation who is excited to apply AI agents to real engineering workflows, learns quickly, and wants to grow into technical leadership in a fast-moving area where model capabilities, tooling, and best practices change month to month.

You're Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…

Build agentic systems that increase the velocity of ML development across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, helping ML engineers get from idea to production model faster.
Design and implement infrastructure that lets agents propose, run, and evaluate modeling experiments.
Build agentic developer support for the ML lifecycle, such as agents that help engineers set up training jobs, debug failing pipelines, review model deployments, and navigate our platform.
Develop evaluation and observability for agent behavior, so we can measure whether agents are actually helping, catch regressions early, and build the trust needed to give them more autonomy.
Work with production standards in mind, including reliability, safety guardrails, cost controls, monitoring, and clear playbooks, so that agentic workflows can run against real ML systems.
Partner closely with ML engineers, data scientists, and platform teams to understand where their time goes and turn those workflows into durable, reusable platform capabilities.
Grow quickly in a fast-moving area, with the chance to shape how agents are used to build and operate ML systems at a company of this scale.

We're Excited About You Because…

B.S., M.S., or PhD in Computer Science or equivalent

A good understanding of how ML engineers and data scientists work, and a track record of building platforms, tools, or services that make them more productive

Experience with agent evaluation, LLM observability, tracing, or building eval harnesses
Experience with ML platforms or MLOps tooling (e.g., Kubeflow, MLflow, Ray, Airflow)

DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. Team Description:

The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. We work hand-in-hand with our partners across the company to advance the state of the art in science and AI engineering, and we build and deploy proprietary solutions that are central to our business and deliver value to millions of customers. Our AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products with the transformative power of AI, in responsible and scalable ways for the highest leverage impact.

What You’ll Do:

Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital One.
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, agents and multi-agent workflows, similarity search, guardrails, model evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc.
Leverage a broad stack of Open Source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, PyTorch, and more.

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist, Seller Merchant
new_jobs.description:
🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!

Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops.

As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact.

We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce.

💻 Role

The Seller Merchant team helps sellers bring inventory onto Whatnot, organize it effectively, and make it easier to sell. That includes products, listings, variants, catalog, taxonomy, inventory creation, seller workflows, and integrations such as Shopify.

Our sellers range from someone going live for the first time on their phone to sophisticated merchants managing large inventories across multiple systems. They also operate across very different categories, countries, and selling formats. The right product experience for one seller may be completely wrong for another.

As a Data Scientist on Seller Merchant, you'll use data to help us understand those differences and build better products for sellers. Your work will ultimately help sellers become more productive, grow their businesses, and bring more high-quality supply to the marketplace.

You'll

Identify and prioritize the highest-impact opportunities to improve seller success. Use product analysis, opportunity sizing, and strategic thinking to understand where changes to seller workflows can have the largest impact on activation, inventory creation, selling efficiency, and GMV.
Design and evaluate experiments across the seller experience. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design to turn ambiguous questions into testable hypotheses, define success metrics and guardrails, design rigorous experiments, and translate results into product decisions.
Develop the analytical frameworks that shape product strategy. Go beyond answering incoming questions by proactively identifying opportunities, defining new ways to measure seller success, and helping the team decide what to build next.
Understand how different sellers need different products. Analyze differences across seller size, maturity, category, country, inventory type, and selling format, and help determine when a single experience works versus when we should build for distinct seller segments.
Help us make good decisions even when the data isn't perfect. Supply-side problems often involve smaller samples, heterogeneous populations, or decisions where data provides important evidence without giving a black-and-white answer. You'll apply analytics, causal inference, and other statistical approaches where appropriate, while partnering closely with product leaders to combine evidence with sound judgment.

You'll be deeply embedded with the product team, but you'll also have meaningful independence to develop your own hypotheses, challenge existing thinking, and use data to influence where the team invests.

We offer flexibility to work from home or from one of our global office hubs, and we value in-person time for planning, problem-solving, and connection. Team members in this role must live within commuting distance of our New York, San Francisco hub.

👋 You

People who do well at Whatnot tend to be comfortable figuring things out as they go, biased toward action, and genuinely curious about what they're building. They care more about outcomes than credit and stay close to the product and the people using it.

As Our Next Data Scientist, You Should Have 5+ Years Of Experience In Product Data Science, Analytics, Or a Closely Related Field, Plus

A Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Mathematics, a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant technical training.
Strong product and business judgment, with experience translating ambiguous product questions into hypotheses, analyses, experiments, and recommendations.
Deep knowledge of experimentation, causal inference, and statistical methods, including approaches appropriate for smaller or noisier datasets such as Bayesian methods.
Strong statistical judgment: you understand what the data can support, what it can't, and when additional product or business judgment is required.
Advanced SQL skills and working proficiency in Python. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable using code to investigate data, perform statistical analysis, and evaluate or debug AI-assisted work.
Experience working closely with Product and Engineering teams and influencing decisions rather than simply delivering analysis.
The ability to disagree constructively: you can push back when the evidence warrants it, communicate uncertainty clearly, and maintain strong working relationships with cross-functional partners.
A track record of independently identifying opportunities and driving analytical work from problem framing through recommendation and impact.

Experience with e-commerce, merchant products, inventory systems, seller tools, or two-sided marketplaces is a plus, but not required.

Bonus signals we look for

You've questioned an existing approach and built something better rather than copying what was done before.
You've owned outcomes end-to-end, not just tasks within a narrow scope.
You've stepped outside your job description to solve a problem because it needed to get done.
You use Whatnot as a buyer or seller and can speak to the product with real context.
You've worked on a marketplace, platform, or product where meaningfully different user groups required different product experiences or analytical approaches.
You've made consequential product recommendations in situations where the data was incomplete, ambiguous, or statistically challenging.

What You'll Get at Whatnot

Compressed career growth. Short feedback loops, real ownership, and problems no one has solved before mean you learn faster. People regularly say one year here equals three elsewhere, and high performers take on more responsibility quickly.
Category-defining work. Live commerce at this scale has never been done in the West. Your work shapes how an entirely new industry develops.
Exceptional colleagues. We're deliberate about talent density. Your coworkers will challenge your thinking, raise your standards, and make you better.
Real ownership. You'll be expected to form opinions, influence decisions, and own outcomes - not just execute a queue of analytical requests.
Tangible seller impact. Sellers are the supply side of our marketplace and are building real businesses on Whatnot. Helping them onboard, operate more efficiently, and grow is fundamental to the company's growth.
Intellectually difficult problems. Seller data is often heterogeneous, sparse, and deeply tied to real-world business behavior. The interesting questions rarely reduce to a single metric or obvious experiment.
AI-forward tools and workflows. We invest in modern AI tools and expect them to be part of daily work. The important skill is increasingly not just writing code, but knowing what questions to ask, moving quickly, and recognizing when the output is, or isn't, trustworthy.
Rewarding collaboration. The work is challenging, but the people are great and wins get celebrated.

🎁 Benefits

Generous Holiday and Time off Policy
Health Insurance options including Medical, Dental, Vision
Work From Home Support
Home office setup allowance
Monthly allowance for cell phone and internet

Care benefits
Monthly allowance for wellness
Annual allowance towards Childcare
Lifetime benefit for family planning, such as adoption or fertility expenses

Retirement; 401k offering for Traditional and Roth accounts in the US (employer match up to 4% of base salary) and Pension plans internationally
Monthly allowance to dogfood the app
All Whatnauts are expected to develop a deep understanding of our product. We're passionate about building the best user experience, and all employees are expected to use Whatnot as both a buyer and a seller as part of their job (our dogfooding budget makes this fun and easy!).

Parental Leave
16 weeks of paid parental leave + one month gradual return to work *company leave allowances run concurrently with country leave requirements which take precedence.

Please note: Whatnot will only contact you through official @whatnot.com email addresses. If you see an email impersonating a Whatnot recruiter, please disregard and report it as spam.

💛 EOE

Whatnot is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diversity, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, parental status, disability status, or any other status protected by local law. We believe that our work is better and our company culture is improved when we encourage, support, and respect the different skills and experiences represented within our workforce.

new_jobs.description:
The Role

This is a client-facing technical role at the intersection of customers, product, and applied AI. You'll work directly with American manufacturers to understand how their business operates, turn messy requirements into clear agent behaviors, and deploy a reliable Frank that delivers measurable value.

You'll own customer agent deployments end-to-end: map workflows, prioritize requirements, write SOPs and prompts, build evals, configure tools and guardrails, launch with users, and improve performance over time. The inputs are real and imperfect: dirty PDFs, legacy data, tribal knowledge, and edge cases that break naive systems.

The work is hands-on, fast-moving, and deeply user-centric. You'll work with LLMs and code every day, communicate directly with customer teams, and turn what you learn in the field into better product capabilities and a faster, more repeatable deployment system.

What You’ll Do

Lead agent deployments from discovery and requirements scoping through configuration, go-live, quantified ROI, and ongoing improvement
Map complex customer workflows and turn them into focused requirements, SOPs, prompts, tools, guardrails, approvals, and handoffs
Build evals and test cases that measure agent quality, expose failure modes, and guide iteration
Configure and launch agents, monitor their real-world performance, investigate failures, and improve reliability over time
Run customer workshops, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and close every dependency and follow-up needed to keep deployments moving
Learn complex customer domains quickly and advocate for customer needs with product and engineering
Turn repeated deployment problems into reusable patterns, tooling, and product improvements that make future launches faster

Who you are

You have 4+ years of experience in software engineering or a client-facing technical role such as forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or implementation consulting
You are technically strong and comfortable writing code, prompting LLMs, building evals, and learning new agent-engineering techniques
You can scope ambiguous requirements, prioritize aggressively, and design a simple solution within real product and operational constraints
You are an exceptional communicator who can run a customer workshop, present with confidence, and build trust from the shop floor to the executive team
You are highly organized and process-oriented: you can manage multiple deployments, track details, use metrics, and close every loop
You learn complex domains quickly and combine customer empathy with a product mindset, turning field insights into better tools and experiences
You are ambitious, resourceful, action-oriented, and team-first; you care about strengthening American manufacturing and are excited to work in person five days a week in NYC and travel to customer sites across the US

Bonus points

Experience building and operating agentic systems in production
Experience in manufacturing or another industrial or operationally complex setting
Experience creating SOPs or leading change-management work
Experience integrating and deploying third-party APIs or legacy systems

About Forgepoint

Revitalize an industry. Rebuild America's manufacturing backbone.

new_jobs.title: Research Scientist – Computer Vision (Body Pose Detection)v1
new_jobs.description:
About Mecka AI

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

The Role

While our existing perception division handles state estimation and spatial mapping, this role is dedicated to one of the most critical bottlenecks in embodied AI: full-body kinematics, human locomotion, and human-scene interaction. We are hiring a Research Scientist to architect and train proprietary foundation models from scratch focused on 3D human body tracking and articulated pose estimation.

Your core mandate is twofold: building our in-house equivalents to cutting-edge 3D human body and mesh recovery architectures, and developing highly robust interaction models tailored for complex, real-world environments characterized by severe occlusions and dynamic motion. Beyond these core pillars, you will serve as a lead problem-solver for emergent perception challenges as our hardware and downstream robotics needs evolve.

To achieve this, we can provide a massive, continuous stream of high-quality, proprietary ground-truth human motion data captured by our infrastructure. You will use this data advantage to train networks that surpass current public baselines, owning the complete human-scene perception loop for our data engine.

What You'll Work On

Architecting Proprietary Articulation Models

Zero-to-One Model Development: Design, implement, and train state-of-the-art networks for 3D human pose estimation, dense full-body mesh recovery, and kinematic tracking.
Large-Scale Distributed Training: Scale multi-view and temporal ML architectures across multi-GPU clusters to handle massive, multi-modal datasets of humans navigating and interacting with their environments.
Loss & Architecture Innovation: Push the boundaries of current paradigms by developing novel loss functions that enforce biomechanical constraints, temporal smoothness, postural balance, and physical plausibility.

Human-Scene Interaction (HSI) & Complex Motion Modeling

Dynamic Scene Understanding: Build and train custom architectures capable of handling extreme motion blur, severe self-occlusion, and multi-person crowding inherent in real-world human behavior.
Allocentric & Egocentric Tracking: Use your models to track human bodies through complex spaces, mapping foot-to-ground contact, joint torques, and environmental affordances to provide rich regularization for downstream action-conditioned robotics models (especially humanoid robots).

Emergent Perception R&D

Rapid Prototyping: Tackle novel, unmapped AI challenges as they arise. You will rapidly prototype and deploy new models for tasks spanning fine-grained action segmentation, intent prediction, and novel hardware sensor integrations.
Agile Problem Solving: Pivot to resolve sudden algorithmic bottlenecks in the data engine, adapting the latest research to unblock new product capabilities for our robotics customers.

Dense Contact & Physics-Aware Tracking

Interaction Integration: Connect the outputs of your foundational tracking models into highly optimized pipelines that reason about physical contact surfaces, gravity, and momentum, directly bridging the gap between human video data and robotic control/locomotion policies.

Who You Are

Required Background

Deep expertise in Deep Learning, 3D Computer Vision, and specifically Articulated Tracking / Human Body Pose Estimation.
Proven experience training large-scale vision models from scratch, not just running inference or fine-tuning existing checkpoints.
Strong theoretical and practical understanding of parametric human body models (e.g., SMPL, SMPL-X, GHUM, MHR, SOMA-X), inverse kinematics, and dense mesh estimation.
Mastery of PyTorch and deep learning scaling frameworks.
Experience handling and curating massive, multi-terabyte image and video datasets for training.
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities can shift rapidly to capitalize on new research or hardware capabilities.

Strong Signals:

First-author publications in top-tier venues (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS) focusing on 3D human pose tracking, human-scene interaction (HSI), human motion capture, or human mesh recovery.
Specific experience working with massive human motion and interaction datasets (e.g., AMASS, Human3.6M, EgoBody, PROX) and solving the unique optimization challenges they present.

Why This Role?

The Data Advantage: You will have access to a scale and quality of proprietary spatial and temporal ground truth for human motion that most academic researchers only dream of.
Pure R&D & Model Ownership: You are not maintaining legacy systems; you are given a blank slate and the compute resources to build the state-of-the-art.
High Impact: The kinematic priors and interaction models you architect will directly define how the next generation of embodied AI agents—from mobile manipulators to humanoid robots—learn to physically navigate, balance, and interact with the world.

Warning:
Research Scientist positions require hyper-specific expertise. Please limit your applications to one research role. Applying to multiple Research Scientist positions suggests a lack of focus and may result in the rejection of all submissions. You may, however, apply to other non-research roles alongside your research application.

A Note on Applying

Studies show women and candidates from underrepresented groups often only apply when they meet 100% of the listed qualifications, while others apply after meeting 60%. If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

Inclusive Hiring at Mecka

We are committed to creating an inclusive and supportive candidate experience. Should you require any accommodation whatsoever during the interview process, please inform us without any hesitation. Mecka is dedicated to ensuring equal treatment and opportunity in all phases of recruitment, selection, and employment, in compliance with employment law. We do not discriminate based on gender, race, religion, national origin, ethnicity, disability, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other protected category. Mecka is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, fostering a culture of inclusivity and maintaining a work environment that is free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

Use of Artificial Intelligence in Recruitment

Mecka uses artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly to support administrative and efficiency-focused aspects of our recruitment process. This includes activities such as drafting job descriptions, generating interview questions, note-taking and recordings, and supporting sourcing and scheduling workflows. All candidate evaluations, interviews, and hiring decisions are made by members of the Mecka team. While AI tools may assist with screening and assessment, they do not replace human judgment in selection decisions. Our use of AI is intended to streamline routine tasks, improve consistency, and enhance the overall candidate experience. We are committed to upholding principles of fairness, transparency, and accountability in all hiring activities. Mecka regularly reviews its recruitment practices to mitigate bias and to ensure alignment with applicable laws and evolving best practices.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, AI
new_jobs.description:
About Us:

At ClarityPay, we’re redefining the point-of-sale credit market to bring more value to merchants. Based in NYC and Atlanta, our fast-growing fintech empowers large merchants with configurable “Pay-Over-Time” tools— including monthly installments, BNPL, and revolving products. We solve complex credit challenges with speed, precision, and intelligence.

Our values guide everything we do: we put merchants first, stay data-driven, always know the why, learn relentlessly, and win together as a team.

Role Overview:

ClarityPay is seeking Forward Deployed Engineers to embed with the teams that run the company and turn how they work into dependable, AI-native systems. You will sit with process owners in finance, credit and portfolio risk, servicing and collections, and operations; scope the problem with them before building; ship agents, controls and automations into production; and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process. You will join the Data & AI organization, working alongside engineers in New York and India on a shared platform, and alongside Product and Engineering you will build external-facing AI solutions for merchants and partners on the ClarityPay platform. You will use AI tooling to make the build the easy part, and you will be measured on what is adopted and relied upon, not on what is demoed.

Key Responsibilities:

Embed with process owners to map how the work actually runs, scope the problem with them before building, and agree success criteria and a baseline up front.
Own delivery end to end — discovery, technical scoping, system design, build and production rollout — and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process.
Choose the simplest dependable solution: simplify or remove a step before automating it, then pick a scheduled job, a triggered job, or a bounded agent with a defined mandate, action set, escalation owner and pause conditions.
Write evaluations for everything you ship: prove the output is correct before a team depends on it, and re-check it as models, data and processes change.
Instrument what you build, and the processes around it, with detective (“day-zero”) controls — thresholds, exception inventories and alerting, each with an action path and a named owner — so a breach surfaces the same day, not at month-end.
Build external-facing AI solutions for merchants and partners with Product and Engineering; anything external ships through Engineering’s review and deployment standards.
Codify reusable patterns, evals and harness standards so the second deployment is faster than the first; prefer reusable capabilities over one agent per task, and bring field signal back to the platform roadmap.
Work inside ClarityPay’s controls for AI — evaluate before exposure, bound the exposure, keep a person at the gate — and propose where a human must review, where automation may act unattended, and what gets logged.
Own the value case: set impact hypotheses and baselines, measure before and after, and report to executives on business impact, total effort saved (including review and maintenance), control quality and reuse.
Continually promote and apply ClarityPay values; be a role model of trust and integrity.

What Success Looks Like in Your First 6–12 Months:

Desktop and spreadsheet-based reporting processes are inventoried, baselined and moved onto AI agentic systems running on governed data, with a person at the gate where judgment is needed.
Recurring performance reporting — portfolio, collections, servicing and finance — is produced by agents from governed metrics rather than manual pulls, on time and traceable to source.
Day-zero controls are live in your first processes, each with a threshold, an action path and a named owner, so breaches surface the same day.
The effort returned is measured against the baseline, net of review, exceptions and maintenance, and reported to executives.
At least one external-facing solution for merchants or partners is in production and adopted.
The patterns, evals and agent-harness standards you built are reused by the next deployment.

Qualifications:

Curious, energetic, positive, solution-oriented, collaborative, trusted.
2–5 years of software engineering or technical deployment experience that includes working directly with business users — in operations, business systems, solutions engineering, or technical consulting.
Production experience with LLMs: prompt engineering, agent or skill development, and evaluation. Things other people depend on, not demos.
Strong Python and SQL: you write and review production code and use AI-assisted development to move faster. Low-code and automation platforms (e.g., Retool, Zapier, n8n) are useful, not a substitute.
Data fluency in a lakehouse environment (e.g., Databricks, ClickHouse): pull answers out of governed data, build reliable pipelines, and catch when the output is wrong.
High agency and comfort with ambiguity — you will choose what to automate as often as you are told.
Strong discovery and communication skills: able to sit with a collections specialist or a finance analyst, understand their workflow, and explain trade-offs to a non-technical audience; comfortable working across time zones with engineering colleagues in India.
Judgment about what should not be automated — where the cost of being wrong outweighs the time saved.

Nice to Have:

Fintech, lending, payments, banking, or another regulated environment.
Experience building MCP servers, sub-agents, or agent skills.
MLOps or experimentation experience: evaluation frameworks, staged A/B tests, model monitoring.
Prior forward-deployed, professional services, or founding-engineer experience.

How You’ll Know This Role Is Right for You:

You see manual, repetitive work and cannot leave it alone.
You would rather ship a working automation this week than design the perfect one this quarter.
You have receipts — things you actually built that other people now depend on.
You want range: collections one month, month-end close the next, portfolio risk monitoring after that.
You would rather stay through adoption than hand off at launch.

What we offer:

Base salary range: $145,000–$195,000, plus variable compensation and equity.
Comprehensive benefits (medical, dental, vision).
401k program.

Ready to redefine point-of-sale financing with us? Apply today and join a passionate team committed to making financial clarity a reality.

, you will help law firm customers transform how legal work gets done with Thomson Reuters Legal AI. Key Responsibilities

In the role of Legal AI Engineer
, you will collaborate closely with Customer Success, Sales, and Product teams to:

Lead in-person discovery sessions, solution demonstrations, workflow workshops, and executive briefings with law firm customers to identify priority legal workflows and show how Thomson Reuters Legal AI can address them.

Required Qualifications

You are a fit for the role of Legal AI Engineer
if you have the following required qualifications:

J.D. from an accredited US law school required.
Prior experience practicing law required (e.g., in a law firm, in-house legal department, government, clerkship, or comparable legal practice setting).

Experience with workflow automation, APIs, integrations, technical prototyping, data analysis, Python, or another form of exploratory coding is strongly preferred.
Experience collaborating with software engineers, solution engineers, implementation teams, or other technical specialists is preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Are comfortable working at the intersection of legal practice and technology, translating ambiguous legal and business needs into structured requirements and testable solutions.

Bring experience or demonstrated aptitude in one or more technically oriented areas, such as workflow automation, system integrations, APIs, data structures, prompt and context design, technical prototyping, or exploratory coding.
Approach challenges constructively, framing Thomson Reuters solutions positively and accurately.
Are knowledgeable in due diligence, eDiscovery, managing large document sets, data rooms, and related workflows where AI can accelerate results.
Excel at communicating technical concepts and creating clear, high-quality documentation and learning materials, and can craft persuasive presentations that resonate with non-technical and often skeptical customers by focusing on their needs and outcomes rather than just product features.
Thrive on working directly with motivated customers to solve complex problems, including through in-person, on-site engagements.
Bring creativity, curiosity, and a growth mindset to problem-solving, with the ability to simplify ambiguous challenges and turn them into opportunities.
Stay up-to-date with emerging AI research and industry trends, and think critically about risks, opportunities, and societal impact.
Embrace innovation and experimentation—you view setbacks as opportunities to learn, iterate, and improve outcomes.

What’s in it For You?

Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. In the United States, Thomson Reuters offers a comprehensive benefits package to our employees. Data Quality & Training: Develop strategies for data curation, filtering, and synthetic data generation to improve training outcomes.
Evaluation & Benchmarking: Design experiments, evaluation frameworks, and benchmarks to measure model performance, identify failure modes, and guide research priorities.

Strong proficiency in Python and PyTorch, JAX, or comparable deep learning frameworks.
Experience designing, executing, and analyzing large-scale machine learning experiments.

new_jobs.title: Specialist Solutions Architect, Radar (Fraud/Risk)
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSA) are domain experts aligned to specific Stripe solutions and customer buying centers. We have in-depth knowledge of specific solution offerings and understanding of customers' challenges. We advise the broader pre-sales team on complex opportunities, support pipeline development and revenue attainment, serve as an advisor on go-to-market sales plays, and provide critical insights to our product and engineering teams.

Stripe Radar is Stripe's fully integrated fraud and risk management platform. The Radar team's mission is to evolve from a best-in-class payment fraud product into a unified risk intelligence platform that protects businesses from all forms of financial loss—from sophisticated payment fraud and account takeovers to first-party misuse and policy abuse. With Radar, businesses can confidently navigate the evolving fraud landscape, accept more good revenue, and focus on growth.

What you'll do

You'll collaborate closely with sales and pre-sales teams to drive pipeline and revenue targets, while also educating the product and engineering teams on market trends and influencing the product roadmap. You'll develop deep relationships with senior customer business leaders and grow Stripe's solution offerings with new and existing customers. As subject matter experts, you'll scale the broader organization by creating reusable assets and coaching others on complex high-value opportunities. You'll also run customer workshops and take the lead on key opportunities. You'll serve as the domain and product expert to our users and GTM team for Stripe Radar globally.

Responsibilities

Act as a subject matter expert on Stripe's Radar product suite to accelerate opportunities globally.
Demonstrate a deep understanding and point of view on trends in the fraud and risk management ecosystem, including AI-powered detection, processor-agnostic architectures, and the shift from payment fraud to holistic business risk (e.g., policy abuse, account takeover, first-party misuse).
Develop expertise with the functional and architectural patterns for deploying advanced fraud systems, including the lifecycle of rule management, ML model tuning, and manual review optimization.
Understand the ecosystem of risk and identity integrations (e.g., device fingerprinting, identity verification, bot mitigation, case management) Stripe must support for our users to be successful.
Define, share, and learn best practices and reusable assets with the broader GTM organization to enhance the quality and efficiency of the team.
Create reference architectures to uplevel the team and refine reference solutions based on product enhancements and feedback from customers.
Partner closely with the Radar product sales team and be an active part of the opportunity team for Stripe's largest and most complex Radar customers to lead strategy and own key customer relationships.
Partner closely with the Radar product team to get early exposure to the new products and features.
Serve as a "Voice of the Customer" internally to drive product and feature request prioritization, providing actionable insights on the competitive landscape and emerging fraud vectors.
Act as an escalation point to drive our most complex technical issues to resolution with Stripe's engineering team.
Support customers and Stripe teammates on account or deal strategy, and answer product feature and technical questions.
Understand the sales process for the product and provide the Sales team with tools and training to qualify potential leads.
Stay current on competitive analysis and market differentiation.
Support marketing events including executive briefings, conferences, user groups, and trade shows.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of experience in a pre-sales, technical consulting, product, or risk strategy role focused on e-commerce fraud prevention, risk management, or trust and safety
Deep working knowledge of the fraud and risk ecosystem, including payment fraud (CNP), account takeover (ATO), first-party misuse (friendly fraud), and policy and content abuse
Demonstrated knowledge of risk management architectures, including the role of rules engines, machine learning models, and manual review queues in fraud decisioning
Strong knowledge of the signals and data used in fraud detection, such as device and IP data, behavioral biometrics, identity verification, and graph-based analysis
Strong knowledge of software engineering and architecture patterns, with the ability to understand how a wide variety of technologies and systems interact with each other
Outstanding communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, comfortable explaining complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
Interest in solving open-ended business problems with a combination of technology and creative thinking
A proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with business partners
Ability to deal effectively with ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment

Preferred Qualifications

Experience integrating Stripe or other RESTful APIs into web applications
Experience with processor-agnostic fraud solutions and multi-processor payment environments
Experience with risk management for various business models, such as platforms and marketplaces, subscription services, and digital goods and SaaS
Familiarity with liability shift programs (e.g., chargeback guarantees) and value-based pricing models for risk products
Understanding of how to extend fraud protection beyond payments to other products like payouts (Issuing), physical payments (Terminal), or recurring billing (Billing)
Experience as a subject matter expert in a relevant industry, vertical, or product

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $184,900 - $277,300. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

new_jobs.description:
Location:
This role requires associates to be in-office 3 days per week, fostering collaboration and connectivity, while providing flexibility to support productivity and work-life balance. This approach combines structured office engagement with the autonomy of virtual work, promoting a dynamic and adaptable workplace. Alternate locations may be considered if candidates reside within a commuting distance from an office.

Please note that per our policy on hybrid/virtual work, candidates not within a reasonable commuting distance from the posting location(s) will not be considered for employment, unless an accommodation is granted as required by law.

The Distinguished AI Engineer
will be responsible for leading the design, development, and deployment of large-scale, production-grade artificial intelligence (AI) systems and platforms that enable enterprise-wide innovation and modernization.

How You Will Make An Impact

Architect and deliver scalable, resilient AI solutions leveraging technologies such as agentic systems, large language models (LLMs), distributed systems, and event-driven architectures.
Define enterprise-wide technical direction, including architecture patterns, integration standards, and reusable platform capabilities.
Lead AI-driven modernization of legacy systems through automated code transformation, service decomposition, and continuous optimization.
Design and implement AI-enabled software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices to improve engineering velocity and quality.
Establish technical standards, governance frameworks, and best practices for AI systems, including monitoring, evaluation, and responsible AI.
Partner with engineering teams and stakeholders to enable adoption of AI-assisted development and drive continuous improvement in system performance and productivity.
Provide technical leadership and mentorship while influencing enterprise technology decisions through deep expertise and hands-on engineering.

Minimum Requirements

Requires a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field and a minimum of 15 years of experience in software engineering, deep expertise in distributed systems and large-scale architecture, or any combination of education and experience, which would provide an equivalent background.
Experience delivering production-grade AI/ML systems at scale, building agentic systems or complex LLM-based applications, modernizing large, complex legacy systems, and delivering high-quality systems also required.
Strong programming expertise in Python, Java, or similar required.
Deep experience with APIs, microservices, and event-driven architectures, cloud platforms, and CI/CD and DevOps practices required.

Preferred Skills, Capabilities And Experiences

Advanced experience designing and leading distributed systems and large-scale architectures is strongly preferred.
Experience establishing enterprise technology standards and influencing technical direction across multiple teams or business domains is preferred.
Experience serving as a technical authority for software engineering practices, architecture, platform strategy, and modern application architectures, including APIs, microservices, cloud technologies, and DevOps practices, is strongly preferred.
Experience delivering production-grade AI/ML systems at scale, building agentic systems or complex LLM-based applications, modernizing large, complex legacy systems, and delivering high-quality systems is preferred.
Strong programming expertise in Python, Java, or similar technology is preferred.
Deep experience with APIs, microservices, and event-driven architectures, cloud platforms, and CI/CD and DevOps practices is preferred.

Elevance Health is a health company dedicated to improving lives and communities – and making healthcare simpler.
